title: Pile of Poo Emoji 💩 Meaning: Why Is the Poop Smiling?
description: The 💩 pile of poo emoji means something is bad, a mild way to say “crap,” or just silly bathroom humor. Learn its Japanese origins and why it has a smile.
summary: The 💩 pile of poo is a brown, swirled dropping with big eyes and a cheerful smile. People use it to call something bad or worthless, as a polite stand-in for “crap” and stronger words, and for silly toilet humor. Its friendly face makes it one of the most lighthearted insults available.
meaning: It replaces a word. “That movie was 💩,” “I feel like 💩,” and “don't give me that 💩” all use the emoji where a swear word would go, and the cartoon smile takes most of the edge off. That makes it handy for criticizing something without sounding truly hostile, and for self-deprecation: “my presentation was 💩.”

The emoji comes from Japan, where it was part of mobile carrier emoji sets before Unicode standardized it in 2010. Poop has a more playful place in Japanese pop culture than in most Western countries, and there is a well-known pun behind it: the word for poop, unko, begins with the same sound as un, meaning luck. Golden poop charms are sold as good-luck novelties for that reason.

Outside Japan it is primarily a joke. Children love it, parents of toddlers use it literally during potty training, and dog owners send it on walks. Friends use it to tease each other, as in “you little 💩.” It became a pop-culture figure in its own right, appearing on cushions, party supplies and as a character in The Emoji Movie.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It is a casual verdict: something is bad, broken or not worth the time. It can also describe a mood or a run of bad luck, as in “today has been 💩.” Among close friends it is an affectionate insult. Literal bathroom updates happen too, mostly between partners, parents and very comfortable friends.

contexts.label: With kids and pets
contexts.body: Families use it without any embarrassment. Messages about diapers, potty-training victories, and whose turn it is to pick up after the dog rely on it. For young children it is simply a funny picture, and it shows up in classroom rewards, toys and birthday themes.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: It stands in for profanity, so apply the same judgment. In a relaxed team, “the wifi is 💩 today” is fine. Calling a person's work 💩 is insulting no matter how cute the icon is, and it has no place in messages to clients.

contexts.label: Around the world
contexts.body: In Japan the image is commonly treated as cute and even lucky, and it appears in children's books and merchandise. In English-speaking countries it is read as mild crude humor or an insult. The same emoji can therefore feel charming in one culture and rude in another.

examples.text: I feel like 💩, staying home today
You little 💩, you ate the last cookie
examples.meaning: Affectionate teasing between people who are close.

examples.text: She went on the potty all by herself! 💩🎉
examples.meaning: A proud parent celebrating a toilet-training milestone.

examples.text: Your turn to walk the dog. Bring bags 💩
examples.meaning: Literal reference to cleaning up after a pet.

combos.meaning: A rebus for “bull” plus the obvious word: calling something nonsense.
Calling something both terrible and ridiculous.
Emphatic: this is truly awful, or pure silliness.

confusedWith.difference: 🍫 is a partly unwrapped chocolate bar. The colors are similar, and people do joke about the resemblance, but the swirl shape and face belong only to 💩.
🤡 mocks a person as foolish. 💩 says a thing, situation or occasionally a person is bad or worthless. One is about stupidity, the other about quality.
🤢 expresses the feeling of disgust or sickness. 💩 names the disgusting thing itself, and is usually humorous where 🤢 can be sincere.

avoid: Do not use it to rate a person's work, cooking or appearance unless you are certain they will laugh.
Avoid it in formal, professional or customer-facing messages.
Skip it while people are eating or discussing food, unless everyone shares that sense of humor.
design: A brown, coiled mound that tapers to a point, with large white eyes and a wide smile. Apple's version closely resembles the swirl of its soft ice cream emoji 🍦. The face was not always standard: Google's early Android design had no eyes or mouth and showed flies circling above it, before being redrawn with the familiar smile.

faqs.q: Why does the poop emoji have a face?
faqs.a: The cheerful face comes from its Japanese origins, where a cute cartoon poop is a common comic image. The smile made the symbol friendly instead of gross, and other companies adopted the same look, which is now standard.

No. Its official name is “pile of poo.” The rumor exists because the swirled shape is close to that of the soft-serve ice cream emoji, especially in Apple's artwork, but it has always represented poop.

faqs.q: What does 💩 mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: There is no gendered meaning. The sender is saying something is bad, joking around, or teasing you. If someone calls you a 💩 with a laughing emoji, it is friendly; without one, they may be annoyed.
Mildly. It is crude humor and a substitute for swearing, but its cartoon style keeps it gentle. It is fine among friends and family and out of place in formal communication.
In Japan it can be. The Japanese word for poop sounds like the word for luck, and golden poop charms are sold as lucky trinkets. Elsewhere the emoji has no such meaning.
